subject.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions

question: Should external agent-session callers be allowed to choose `contextOverflowRecoveryOwner`, or should provider-authoritative recovery remain an embedded-runner-only implementation detail?
rationale: This is a durable plugin SDK and session-recovery policy decision; source-level correctness cannot determine whether exposing that control is an intended supported contract.

options.title: Keep recovery ownership internal
options.body: Remove the public SDK option and pass the caller/session ownership decision through an internal embedded-runner seam, preserving one supported external session behavior.

options.title: Approve and support the SDK option
options.body: Retain the option only with explicit owner approval, documented semantics, compatibility expectations, and focused public-SDK coverage.

options.title: Pause for policy design
options.body: Defer this broader branch until maintainers decide the long-term provider-authoritative recovery contract across session callers.

recommendation.title: Keep recovery ownership internal
recommendation.body: Remove the public SDK option and pass the caller/session ownership decision through an internal embedded-runner seam, preserving one supported external session behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the most direct current implementation context, though the final API-direction decision requires an established agent-runtime owner.
